blocks.value: Scanner (from java.util) reads data from the keyboard into variables. Import it, then create a Scanner object connected to standard input:

import java.util.Scanner;

Scanner input = new Scanner(System.in);
input is just a variable name you choose; System.in is the input stream connected to the keyboard. Each value Scanner reads is called a token, a chunk of characters separated by whitespace.

Method        Reads as
nextInt()     int
nextDouble()  double
nextFloat()   float
nextLong()    long
nextShort()   short
nextByte()    byte
next()        String (one token)
nextLine()    String (the whole line)

If the next token doesn't match the expected type, these methods throw an exception. There's no method for reading a single char directly. Call next() to get a String token, then charAt(0) to grab its first character: input.next().charAt(0)
